title: What someone said
verifiedBy: LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: REPORTING MOVES THE TENSE BACK ONE STEP, ONTO L2-M10's IMPARFAIT. il dit qu'il vient becomes il a dit qu'il venait; elle dit qu'elle ne peut pas becomes elle a dit qu'elle ne pouvait pas. Nothing new is opened for the tense — it is the imparfait you already have, sitting in a second seat. English does the same shift (he said he was coming), so the machinery transfers; what does not transfer is that French will not leave the present there.

A YES/NO QUESTION IS REPORTED WITH si AND NEVER WITH que. il m'a demandé si j'avais le temps — the same si L3-M4 taught for conditions, doing a second job, and it does NOT fuse here unless il follows it. que reports a STATEMENT and nothing else; a learner who uses it for a question has written something French does not have. A wh-question keeps its own word instead: où, quand, pourquoi, comment.

A REQUEST IS NOT A CLAUSE AT ALL: it becomes de plus an infinitive. il m'a dit d'attendre, il m'a demandé de venir. English keeps the verb whole too (he told me to wait), but it uses to, and French uses de — the one preposition L3-M2's modals were forbidden. After dit and demandé it is required.

THE OBJECT PRONOUNS ARE SPELLED EXACTLY LIKE L1-M1's ARTICLES AND GO BEFORE THE VERB. le, la and les are the article in front of a noun and the object in front of a verb, and the word never changes shape to tell you which it is: je les connais against les livres. English puts the object AFTER the verb (I know them), so the position is the whole delta, and this module teaches each one glued to its verb rather than on its own.

lui AND leur ARE THE INDIRECT OBJECT — to him, to her, to them — AND THEY DO NOT SHOW GENDER. je lui ai parlé is I spoke to him or to her, with nothing in the sentence to say which; je leur ai parlé is the plural. le, la and les are the direct object and do show it. English marks the gender and drops the to; French drops the gender and keeps the to inside the word.

THE PARTICIPLE AGREES WITH A DIRECT OBJECT THAT COMES BEFORE IT, AND WITH NOTHING ELSE ON avoir — AND IT IS A WRITING-ONLY RULE. je l'ai vue (a woman), je les ai vus (men), je les ai vues (women). Say the limit as loudly as the rule: j'ai vu la voiture has the object AFTER the participle and takes no agreement at all, and neither does je lui ai parlé, because lui is indirect. Every one of those endings is silent, so a learner hears nothing and must write it.
THE ne IS STILL WRITTEN, INSIDE THE REPORTED CLAUSE TOO. elle a dit qu'elle ne pouvait pas venir — speech drops it and writing keeps it, exactly as in every module before this one.

sentences.display: Il a dit qu'il venait ce soir
sentences.cue: He said he was coming this evening
sentences.literal: He has said that-he was-coming this evening

words.note: L1-M9's que elided onto the pronoun and written as one word. It happens before every vowel: qu'il, qu'elle, qu'on — never que il.
L1-M10's venir in L2-M10's imparfait. Reporting is what puts it here: il dit qu'il vient, il a dit qu'il venait.

sentences.trap: The reported verb moves back even when the arrangement still stands. il a dit qu'il vient looks reasonable and is not what a French speaker writes — the step back is automatic, not a comment on whether he is still coming.
sentences.sound: eel a dee keel vuh-NEH suh SWAR. qu'il is one syllable, keel.

variations.display: Elle a dit qu'elle venait ce soir
variations.cue: She said she was coming this evening
variations.changed: elle, so que elides onto her instead

variations.display: Il dit qu'il vient ce soir
variations.cue: He says he's coming this evening
variations.changed: the present on both sides, so nothing steps back

mistake.display: Il a dit qu'il vient ce soir
mistake.why: Reporting steps the verb back: Il a dit qu'il venait ce soir.

sentences.usage: Passing on an arrangement somebody else made, which is what most reporting is.
sentences.mnemonic: Said in the past, told in the imparfait.

sentences.display: Elle a dit qu'elle ne pouvait pas venir
sentences.literal: She has said that-she not could not to-come

words.note: L2-M1's peux in the imparfait, and the shape reporting needs: elle dit qu'elle ne peut pas, elle a dit qu'elle ne pouvait pas.

sentences.trap: The ne and pas still wrap the modal, inside the reported clause exactly as outside it, and the ne is still written. qu'elle pouvait pas is what you will hear and is not what you write.
sentences.sound: el a dee kel nuh poo-VEH pa vuh-NEER.

variations.display: Il a dit qu'il ne pouvait pas venir
variations.cue: He said he couldn't come
variations.changed: il, so que elides onto him

variations.display: Elle a dit qu'elle voulait rester
variations.cue: She said she wanted to stay
variations.changed: L3-M4's voulait, stepped back the same way

mistake.display: Elle a dit qu'elle peut pas venir
mistake.why: Two things: the verb steps back, and the ne is written. Elle a dit qu'elle ne pouvait pas venir.

sentences.usage: Passing on a refusal, which is the reporting a learner needs first.
sentences.mnemonic: The negative reports whole — ne included.

sentences.display: Il m'a demandé si j'avais le temps
sentences.cue: He asked me if I had time
sentences.literal: He me-has asked if I-had the time

words.note: L2-M5's m' fused onto a and written as one word. The pronoun comes BEFORE the auxiliary in a passé composé: il m'a demandé, never il a demandé moi.
It means asked a question or asked for something — never demanded, which is exigé. The false friend is one of the loudest French has.

sentences.trap: A reported yes/no question takes si and never que. Il m'a demandé QUE j'avais le temps is the sentence English word order builds and it is not French; si is L3-M4's word doing a second job here.
sentences.sound: eel ma duh-mahn-DAY see zha-VEH luh TAHN.

variations.display: Il m'a demandé si tu étais libre
variations.cue: He asked me if you were free
variations.changed: the question is about you, so the clause steps back on tu

variations.display: Elle m'a demandé si j'avais le temps
variations.cue: She asked me if I had time
variations.changed: elle asking instead

mistake.display: Il m'a demandé que j'avais le temps
mistake.why: que reports a statement; a yes/no question takes si: Il m'a demandé si j'avais le temps.

sentences.usage: Reporting a phone call, where a question and an answer both need passing on.

sentences.display: Il m'a demandé quand tu partais
sentences.cue: He asked me when you were leaving
sentences.literal: He me-has asked when you were-leaving

words.note: L1-M6's partir in the imparfait. Reporting steps tu pars back to tu partais, on the same endings as every other imparfait.

sentences.trap: A wh-question keeps its own word and nothing else changes: quand, où, pourquoi, comment. Only the yes/no kind needs si, and only a statement takes que — three shapes, and picking the wrong one is the module's whole error surface.
sentences.sound: eel ma duh-mahn-DAY kahn tü par-TEH.

variations.display: Il m'a demandé où tu travaillais
variations.cue: He asked me where you worked
variations.changed: a different question word, same shape after it

variations.display: Il m'a demandé pourquoi tu partais
variations.cue: He asked me why you were leaving
variations.changed: pourquoi, and the clause untouched

mistake.display: Il m'a demandé si quand tu partais
mistake.why: A question word replaces si rather than joining it: Il m'a demandé quand tu partais.

sentences.usage: Relaying somebody else's question, which is half of being in the middle of a plan.
sentences.mnemonic: The question word is the joint.

sentences.cue: He told me to wait here

words.note: de plus attendre, elided into one written word. English uses to for this and French uses de — the preposition L3-M2's modals refused is the one a request requires.

sentences.trap: A request never becomes a que clause. Il m'a dit que j'attends is not the sentence; an order or a request collapses into de plus an infinitive, and the person it is aimed at is already there in the m'.
sentences.sound: eel ma dee da-TAHNDR ee-SEE. The final re is barely a sound.

variations.display: Elle m'a dit d'attendre
variations.cue: She told me to wait
variations.changed: elle giving the instruction, and nowhere named

variations.display: Il m'a demandé d'attendre ici
variations.cue: He asked me to wait here
variations.changed: demandé, which softens an order into a request

mistake.display: Il m'a dit à attendre ici
mistake.why: The preposition is de: Il m'a dit d'attendre ici.

sentences.usage: Explaining why you are standing where you are, which is this sentence's real job.
sentences.mnemonic: An order takes de, not a clause.

sentences.display: Je l'ai vue hier au marché
sentences.cue: I saw her yesterday at the market
sentences.literal: I her-have seen yesterday at-the market

words.note: The l' is la or le, elided — the object, not L1-M1's article. It sits BEFORE the verb, and the participle takes an e when it stands for a woman.

sentences.trap: The l' is spelled exactly like the article and is not one. le livre is a book; je l'ai vu is I saw it — same two letters, and only the position tells you, because a French object pronoun goes in FRONT of the verb where English puts it behind.
sentences.sound: zhuh lay VÜ ee-YEHR o mar-SHAY. vue and vu are the same sound; only the page separates them.

variations.display: Je l'ai vu hier au marché
variations.cue: I saw him yesterday at the market
variations.changed: a man, so the participle loses its e — and nothing is heard

variations.display: J'ai vu ma sœur hier
variations.cue: I saw my sister yesterday
variations.changed: the object after the verb, so there is no agreement at all

mistake.display: J'ai vu la hier au marché
mistake.why: The object goes before the verb and elides: Je l'ai vue hier au marché.

sentences.usage: Answering a question about somebody the other person has just named.
sentences.mnemonic: The object goes first, the e goes silent.

sentences.display: Je les ai vus au restaurant
sentences.cue: I saw them at the restaurant

words.note: les is the plural object here, not L1-M1's article, and the participle takes s for them and es for a group of women. Both endings are silent.

sentences.trap: This is the writing-only rule at its clearest. vu, vus and vues are one sound; the learner hears a single word and has to choose between three spellings from what the object was — which is why an ear will never supply it.
sentences.sound: zhuh lay-zay VÜ o res-to-RAHN. The s of les links onto ai as a z.

variations.display: Je les ai vues au restaurant
variations.cue: I saw them at the restaurant
variations.changed: a group of women, so the participle takes es — still silent

variations.display: J'ai vu mes amis au restaurant
variations.cue: I saw my friends at the restaurant
variations.changed: the object named after the verb, so no agreement

mistake.display: Je les ai vu au restaurant
mistake.why: A direct object in front of the participle makes it agree: Je les ai vus au restaurant.

sentences.usage: Reporting a sighting, which is what a whole evening's account is made of.
sentences.mnemonic: Object in front, ending on the back.

sentences.display: Je lui ai parlé ce matin
sentences.cue: I spoke to him this morning
sentences.literal: I to-him have spoken this morning

words.cue: I spoke to him · I spoke to her
words.note: The to is inside lui, so parler needs no preposition after it. The participle does NOT agree, because lui is indirect.
One word for both genders: nothing in je lui ai parlé says whether it was a man or a woman. English marks the gender and French marks the direction instead.

sentences.trap: No agreement here, and that is the limit of the rule rather than an exception to it. lui is indirect, so parlé stays flat — a learner who has just met je l'ai vue will want to write parlée, and there is nothing to agree with.
sentences.sound: zhuh lwee ay par-LAY suh ma-TAN. lui is one syllable, lwee.

variations.display: Je lui ai parlé hier
variations.cue: I spoke to her yesterday
variations.changed: a different day — and still nothing to say which of them it was

variations.display: Je l'ai vue ce matin
variations.cue: I saw her this morning
variations.changed: a direct object, so the participle agrees after all

mistake.display: Je lui ai parlée ce matin
mistake.why: lui is indirect, so nothing agrees: Je lui ai parlé ce matin.

sentences.usage: Saying you have already dealt with somebody, which is what closes an arrangement.
sentences.mnemonic: lui carries the to and blocks the agreement.

sentences.display: Je les connais bien, ce sont mes amis
sentences.cue: I know them well, they're my friends
sentences.literal: I them know well, these are my friends

words.note: The object still goes before the verb in the present: je les connais, never je connais les. The verb is for knowing PEOPLE and places rather than facts.

sentences.trap: English puts the object after the verb and cannot do otherwise — I know them — so the French order has nothing to attach to and is the error a learner makes for months. There is no participle here at all, which means no agreement to worry about either.
sentences.sound: zhuh lay ko-NEH byan, suh son may-za-MEE. The final s of connais is silent.

variations.display: Je le connais bien
variations.cue: I know him well
variations.changed: one man, so les becomes le

variations.display: Je la connais, c'est ma collègue
variations.cue: I know her, she's my colleague
variations.changed: one woman, so les becomes la

mistake.why: The object pronoun goes in front of the verb: Je les connais bien.

sentences.usage: Vouching for people you have just been asked about.
sentences.mnemonic: The pronoun goes where English will not put it.

sentences.display: Je leur ai parlé hier au téléphone
sentences.cue: I spoke to them yesterday on the phone
sentences.literal: I to-them have spoken yesterday at-the telephone

words.note: The plural of je lui ai parlé, and it takes no s — leur is already plural here. The participle stays flat, as it does after any indirect object.
Two different words are spelled leur: this one, to them, never takes an s, while leur meaning their does — leurs amis. Position tells them apart.

sentences.trap: leur before a verb is to them and never takes an s. The possessive leur, in front of a noun, does take one — so the same four letters are invariable in one place and inflected in the other, and only what follows tells you which.
sentences.sound: zhuh lur ay par-LAY ee-YEHR o tay-lay-FON.

variations.display: Je leur ai parlé ce matin
variations.cue: I spoke to them this morning
variations.changed: a different time, and still no agreement

variations.display: Je lui ai parlé hier au téléphone
variations.cue: I spoke to him yesterday on the phone
variations.changed: one person, so leur becomes lui

mistake.display: Je leurs ai parlé hier au téléphone
mistake.why: The pronoun leur never takes an s: Je leur ai parlé hier au téléphone.

sentences.usage: Closing an account of a day's messages, which is where every shape in this module turns up at once.
sentences.mnemonic: leur to a verb is bare; leur to a noun can grow an s.
